strengths: Well-motivated problem with strong empirical evidence (Figure 2) showing Hessian error correlates with phonon property errors across multiple MLIP architectures
Technically sound scalable solution using Hessian-vector products reduces computational complexity from O(N²) to O(N), enabling training on large supercells required for accurate phonon calculations

Substantial and convincing experimental results: 55% average error reduction on phonon properties, state-of-the-art thermal conductivity predictions (κSRME 0.306 vs. baseline 0.446), and generalization to third-order derivatives
Thoughtful co-training strategy effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting with <1% degradation on Matbench Discovery F1 score (Figure 3), preserving downstream task performance
Comprehensive evaluation including phonon band structures, thermal conductivity, elastic properties, and stability classification; rigorous comparison with recent MLIP foundations models
Excellent reproducibility: clear algorithm description, detailed hyperparameter justification (Table A.1), code/data release promised, and honest limitations discussion
weaknesses: Limited architectural scope: thoroughly evaluated only on Nequix MP; broader claims of 'model agnostic' utility unsupported by direct evaluation on MACE, SevenNet, or other architectures; symmetry-aware sampling requires E(3)-equivariance with unclear generalization to non-equivariant models

Substantial dataset mismatch (31.60 meV/atom energy difference between MDR Phonon and MPtrj) is acknowledged but unresolved; this likely contributes to ~30 meV/atom energy MAE and unclear implications for learned Hessians; relatively small phonon dataset (~9,000 novel materials) limits scale assessment

Co-training introduces significant hyperparameter complexity with minimal justification: co-training ratio K=4 lacks systematic sensitivity analysis and principled selection beyond 'trade-off' argument; no ablation on co-training hyperparameters

Incomplete theoretical understanding: intriguing observation that EFS training on displacement data worsens Hessian error (Section 3.2) is stated but unexplained; limited analysis of which phonon properties benefit most and why Hessian errors correlate with different properties

Mixed results on non-phonon tasks undermine generality claims: no improvement on Matbench Discovery stability (Table 3), degraded bulk modulus predictions (Table A.2), suggesting PFT may harm other property predictions despite co-training

Limited ablation studies: no systematic variation of force constant weight λΦ, no comparison beyond Table 1 for analytical vs. finite-displacement Hessians, missing analysis of column sampling variance and optimal strategies for stochastic Hessian training

Practical computational concerns underexplored: 'triple-backward' mentioned but not analyzed as potential bottleneck; inference cost not provided; 60-140 A100 hours for fine-tuning still substantial; no wall-clock time comparison with alternative approaches

strengths: Strong empirical results: 55% average error reduction on phonon properties, achieving state-of-the-art for MPtrj-trained models
Scalable methodology: Stochastic Hessian-vector product efficiently reduces complexity from O(N²) to O(N), enabling training on large supercells
Practical utility: Uses data already generated in standard DFT workflows; only 35 A100 hours training cost

Thorough experimental evaluation: Comprehensive ablations demonstrating necessity of each component, tests across multiple base models (Nequix, MACE), and unexpected finding that direct displacement training fails badly
Generalization: Improvements extend to third-order force constants (20-30% reduction) and thermal conductivity (31% improvement) without explicit training
Reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters provided, code/models/data release promised, clear ablation studies enable reproduction
Model-agnostic: Demonstrated effectiveness across different architectures, not limited to single model type
Honest limitations discussion: Out-of-equilibrium configurations, non-equivariant architecture constraints, and dataset mismatch issues acknowledged
weaknesses: Energy mismatch between datasets (31.60 meV/atom between MDR Phonon and MPtrj) inadequately addressed; relegated to appendix despite potentially affecting results and requiring zero force/stress assumptions

Limited theoretical understanding: Why direct displacement training fails dramatically is observed but not explained; receptive field argument (Sec 3.5) insufficiently developed; stochastic sampling convergence analysis absent

Generalization uncertainty: All experiments use Materials Project data with ~99% overlap between MPtrj and MDR Phonon; OAM training includes MPtrj, limiting independence; no testing on structurally different datasets

Specialized impact: Results primarily benefit phonon predictions; Matbench Discovery stability shows negligible improvements; elastic properties mixed (bulk modulus worsens), limiting claim of general MLIP improvement
Arbitrary hyperparameter choices: Co-training ratio K=4 based on GPU budget rather than principled tuning; test set construction rationale unclear; learning rate selection lacks specificity
Limited comparison with related work: Recent Hessian-based approaches (Fang et al. 2024, Amin et al. 2025) mentioned but not compared empirically; distinction from prior art could be clearer
Column sampling justification: While Appendix A.1 shows empirical speedup, theoretical analysis of uniform random sampling optimality relative to symmetry-aware alternatives is absent

Incomplete analysis: Failure modes not discussed; minimum phonon data requirements unclear; quantitative comparison between analytical and finite displacement methods mentioned as 'near identical' but specifics missing
